card.title: Playstation 3

claims.statement: PS3 model reference: CECHA/B have full PS2 hardware; CECHC/E partial; CECHG is the last NAND-firmware model and CECHH the first NOR; CECHJ introduced the 65 nm RSX and CECHL a revised 65 nm RSX (CXD2991GB) and new board layout.
Slim and Super Slim board revisions: CECH-20xx DYN-001, 21xx SUR-001, 25xx JTP/JSD-001, 30xx KTE-001; 40xx MPX/MSX/NPX-001, 42xx NPX/PPX/PQX-001, 43xx RTX/REX-001.
8002F14E / dead Blu-ray: check the Blu-ray drive IC, daughterboard and nearby fuses; laggy XMB/freezes usually means a failing HDD (check SMART on a direct SATA port).

YLOD can be a bad RSX (bumps or solder balls, mostly 90 nm), or bad NEC/Tokin capacitors; read syscon error codes via UART before repairing. Bump failures need an RSX replacement—consider a 40 nm RSX.
Replacing NEC/Tokins: 0E128 use 470 µF ×4 each, 0E108 use 330 µF ×4 each (MacBook 820-2850 caps suggested); jumper positive ends if all four are replaced because the originals bridge internally.

procedure: Identify model/board from the CECH number.
For YLOD, solder UART to syscon and read error codes.
Power errors: replace NEC/Tokins; RSX errors: reflow/reball or replace RSX.
card.caveats: Community-written Repair Wiki page, paraphrased; check the linked page (and its images) before acting on a reading.
